title: X-ray Chest - Adult

description: Published structure and wording of the X-ray Chest (Adult) national referral criteria, with each criterion bound to a named expression in the CQL library CRR_XRChest_Adult. NOT CLINICALLY REVIEWED (staging demo, AD-35). This resource carries what the Criteria Viewer renders; the Library carries the logic; the Questionnaire carries the input contract. The 'Refer for acute assessment without initial imaging' row is shown for display only: it is evaluated by the national red-flag library CRR_RedFlags (RF-14 to RF-17).

action.title: Guidance
action.description: In patients with an acute lower respiratory tract infection a chest x-ray does not change the management in most cases.

documentation.label: National criteria v2.0, p.62 — Guidance box (printed beside the Acute: Within 24 hours row)

action.title: Refer for acute assessment without initial imaging.
Haemoptysis with “red flags” including if
Significant (e.g., more than 20ml (1 tablespoon) in a single episode) or life threatening (e.g., more than 100 ml/hour) haemoptysis
Haemodynamically unstable
Haemoptysis with hoarseness or stridor
Acute dyspnoea and/or chest pain
Severe respiratory distress
Suspected large pneumothorax with significant pain, breathlessness, tachycardia
Suspected active Tuberculosis and the patient is acutely unwell – follow the Tuberculosis pathway
